verified: The study is a peer-reviewed article in Social Science & Medicine (vol. 410, 2026) by Yi-Chun Ko of the Asian Growth Research Institute and Shinsuke Uchida of Doshisha University, and journal indexes confirm its stated scope — whether residential solar PV can mitigate health risks by reducing households' reliance on grid electricity during extreme heat (tool-2-1, tool-2-3); its publication listing dates to October 2026 (tool-2-2).
unconfirmed: The headline figures — an ~8.2% annual reduction in heat-related excess deaths overall and ~8.5% for people 65 and older — are the authors' own model-based estimates from their instrumental-variable design, not independently replicated measurements, and the "first causal evidence" description is the co-author's characterization of his own work; the 38% electricity price increase and the prefecture-level mortality and installation data are stated in the paper without independent verification here, and the authors themselves note that solar adoption skews toward higher-income households, so the size and distribution of any real-world benefit remain uncertain.

verified: 这篇论文题为《Climate resilience through residential solar energy: Reducing health risks from extreme temperatures》，作者为亚洲成长研究所的 Yi-Chun Ko 与日本同志社大学的 Shinsuke Uchida，刊于《Social Science & Medicine》第 410 卷（2026 年），ScienceDirect 与 RePEc 的文献记录均与其一致；研究以 2011 年东日本大地震后核电停运、电价最高上涨 38% 并同期推行住宅光伏补贴为自然实验，将 2009—2014 年 44 个都道府县的月度死亡率数据、天气数据与官方光伏装机数据结合，用工具变量法分离光伏 adopt 的影响，结论是极端高温相关超额死亡年均减少约 8.2%，65 岁及以上人群约 8.5%，低温下未见类似效应。
unconfirmed: 8.2% 与 8.5% 是作者按研究期内光伏装机年均增速推算的模型估计值，并非实测的死亡人数下降，尚无独立复现或第三方评估；作者所称这是“首个证明户用光伏可作为公共卫生干预手段的因果证据”，属于作者自我评价，未获外部确认；研究结论基于日本特定电价冲击与补贴环境，能否外推到其他市场、其他电价机制尚不清楚；论文也自认光伏 adoption 偏向高收入地区，健康收益分配可能不均，这一点尚无量化数据支撑。
